thread:
matt: Heads up — during the DR bulk snapshot run this morning we hit two related limits in us-west-2: account EBS volume count is at the soft limit and snapshot copy throughput is getting throttled. AWS console shows a spike of failed snapshot copy ops and some fsync stalls on a few nodes.

sarah: ugh, timeline? is this impacting prod traffic or batch jobs?

matt: batch backup only right now but it's blocking our migration testing. some worker VMs had long pauses (~30s) while committing, so we want the quotas bumped before we re-run.

raj: do we know which quotas exactly? AWS has separate quotas for "Snapshot copy rate" and "Total EBS volumes" per region. also gp3 IOPS vs throughput could be relevant if we're provisioning many high-iops volumes.

matt: I captured the console errors — AWS case shows: "Exceeded snapshot copy throughput (RateExceed)" and UI flagged "EBS volumes: 240 / 240 (soft limit)". our target for the migration is ~320 volumes in us-west-2.

emily: cost question — if we just bump to 320 volumes and provisioned iops, we'll increase monthly spend. can we instead reduce concurrency of snapshot jobs or stage them?

matt: yes, we can stagger, but that slows migration by days. customer timeline wants it sooner. prefer temporary quota increase for 2 weeks + stagger fallback.

raj: also check snapshot copy cross-region (us-west-2 -> us-east-1) egress. GCS/ S3 transfer limits can bite when copying many snapshots at once. are we using fast snapshot copy or creating snapshots then copying?

matt: we do snapshot -> copy to target region for DR. seen API throttles on the CopySnapshot calls.

cloudops-bot: [alert] snapshot-copy-throttle detected: region=us-west-2, metric=SnapshotCopyOpsThrottled, window=5m, count=73 :rotating_light:

emily: can we use EBS direct APIs to stream snapshots to S3 and then cross-region replicate? Might avoid CopySnapshot throttles but adds integration work.

raj: short term: request increase for two quotas: "EBS volumes per region" to 400 and "Snapshot copy rate" to X per second (recommend asking support for 5rps sustained). also request temporary increase to gp3 baseline throughput if we plan concurrent heavy IO.

sarah: please include exact numbers and justification in the support case: current business impact, timeline (2 weeks), and rollback plan. infra-support, can you draft the case?

infra-support: drafting now. suggested body: "Requesting temporary quota increases in us-west-2: EBS volumes from 240->400, SnapshotCopyOps from 2/s->5/s sustained, and EBS Snapshots Bandwidth to accommodate bulk migration. Impact: migration of 80 additional volumes for customer X; without increase migration will be delayed >72h. Will revert to previous levels after 2026-05-05. Contact: matt@redwood.com." want to add cost estimate?

matt: add cost note: ~+$1,200/mo if we keep increases but we'll limit to 2 weeks — include projected one-off data transfer: ~3TB cross-region => ~$300. mention we're willing to accept temporary higher charges.

emily: add fallback plan: staggered snapshot schedule with 8 parallel jobs and 30s gap to avoid triggering throttles. include runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/snapshot-migration.

raj: also request a soft limit for concurrent volume attachments? we saw errors when many workers attached simultaneously. maybe request "AttachVolume API rate" increase to 10rps.

infra-support: added attach rate request and sample CloudWatch graphs. I'll file now. drafting ticket subject: "Quota increase request: EBS volumes, SnapshotCopyOps, AttachVolume rate — us-west-2 — migration"

matt: thanks. can you post the AWS case ID here once submitted? also tag accounts: prod-redwood-usw2 and migrations-redwood.

infra-support: submitted. AWS case 12345678912 — category: Service Quotas / EBS. ETA from AWS: 48-72 hours.

cloudops-bot: [info] case 12345678912 created by infra-support, priority: High, linked to account prod-redwood-usw2.

sarah: good. who will run the next snapshot attempt and monitor throttles?

matt: raj and I will run a small test window tonight with reduced concurrency. we'll record CloudWatch metrics and post results. if metrics look clean, we'll schedule full run after AWS confirms.

raj: action items: 1) infra-support monitor case and escalate if no response in 36h; 2) matt/raj run 2-hour trial tonight at 11pm PST; 3) emily prepare cost/rollback note for finance. I'll add a CloudWatch alarm for SnapshotCopyOpsThrottled > 10 in 5m.

emily: got it. finance pinged and ok with temporary transfer costs.

matt: thanks all — I'll update here after test and when AWS responds. :thumbsup:

infra-support: noted. case link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=12345678912

raj: one more note — if AWS can't increase SnapshotCopyOps quickly, fallback is using incremental snapshots + accelerate copy window with reduced concurrency. will document script.

matt: perfect. end of thread.
